summary: Update check: the packaged app asks GitHub for the latest release (cached 6 h, switch in Settings), shows a quiet strip on the main page, downloads the platform installer into <data>/updates/ with SHA-256 verification, and after the app quit starts the Windows installer or replaces the macOS .app (with rollback; manual Finder fallback).
scope_note: Worktree update-check, base main 36d2070. New outbound network access (GitHub only) registered in ARCHITECTURE and ADR 0041; launching a downloaded file is the critical path. Release workflow already produces the asset names the check needs (verified by reading, no change).

budget_impact.rationale: No model call, prompt, retry or token. One public GET to api.github.com at most every 6 hours (switchable) and a user-initiated asset download; no user data in any request.
budget_impact.after: optional GitHub release check and user-initiated installer download

additional_checks.command: cargo check --offline (empty placeholder resources dir, CARGO_TARGET_DIR in TMPDIR)
additional_checks.scope: Rust shell compiles on macOS; the Windows cfg path is unchanged by this commit

open_risks: No request was ever made to the real GitHub API or CDN (sandbox denies it); response shapes follow the documented API and are tested with a fake transport.
The Windows PowerShell helper and the installer takeover, and the macOS replacement script on a real signed-less .app (Gatekeeper, translocation), have not run on real hardware.
release.yml and RELEASE.md asset names were checked by reading only.
